record.title: Exact inverse frame-cycle normalization from shared-event Tick ownership
record.one_line_meaning: For the same declared event/window, a native rate ratio G=omega_i/omega_J implies raw i-cycle count nG in n J ticks, but conversion into J-cycle-equivalent units is exactly N_norm=N_raw/G; the inverse 1/G is unit/frame normalization, not detector attenuation.
formal_core: Let frame J own calibrated Tick duration tau_J and layer/frame i own tau_i. For the same cycle event class, omega_i/omega_J=tau_J/tau_i=:G_{i:J}>0.
For a J-owned window W_J=n tau_J, the raw number of i cycles is N_i^raw=W_J/tau_i=n G_{i:J}.
One i cycle has duration tau_i=(tau_J/G_{i:J}), so expressed in J-cycle-equivalent units its value is tau_i/tau_J=1/G_{i:J}. Therefore N_{i->J}^norm=N_i^raw/G_{i:J}=n.

Hence the frame-cycle normalization coefficient is exactly boxed D_{i:J}^norm=1/G_{i:J}. It follows from inverse unit conversion after event/window and Tick ownership are fixed; it is not an independent dynamical suppression law.
Composition is exact: G_{A:C}=G_{A:B}G_{B:C} implies D_{A:C}^norm=D_{A:B}^norm D_{B:C}^norm=1/G_{A:C}.

Coordinate-base invariance is exact: for any valid logarithmic base b, x_b=log_b G, G=b^{x_b}, and D_norm=b^{-x_b}=1/G. The base changes the coordinate only, not the represented ratio or inverse normalization.
Turbo-Onion count-only provenance independently contains the same algebraic structure: for one shared closure event with fixed mark count M and s=T_in/T_out, rates M/T satisfy (M/T_in)/(M/T_out)=1/s.
guardrails: Frame-cycle normalization is not physical detector attenuation, coupling loss, geometric shrinkage, or range suppression.

A raw gate/event counter that resolves every native cycle returns nG over n observer ticks, not n. The normalized result n is obtained only after expressing the raw count in observer-owned cycle units.
Same event class, explicit Tick owners, and an explicit comparison window are mandatory; mismatched events/windows invalidate the inverse conversion claim.
This node does not derive the physical origin of G. In particular, it does not resolve why g21=2^x21 physically owns the native L2/L1 rate.
